content.text:
# Firstmate 3000 — Design System

Firstmate 3000 is an AI assistant for software development and general knowledge work, shipped as an Electron desktop app (light + dark theme, dark default). The product feeling: **calm, peaceful, confident, futuristic, a bit of space-travel fantasy, minimal, distraction-free**.

## Product concepts
- **The input** — the default state of the app is a single text input. Placeholder: `press/hold [keybind] to talk` (default keybind: hold right ⌥; configurable). Activated, it becomes a live waveform with three controls: abandon (left end), accept, submit (rightmost).
- **Firstmate** — the character. A 4D wireframe structure (tesseract projection) of lines and dots with a pair of soft-light eyes in the inner cell (blinking, gaze wandering when idle), continuously animating under an explicit state machine (captain-approved spec: `firstmate/data/fm3000-character-animation-prototypes-s1/report.md`; the app's `src/renderer/src/character/` is the reference implementation — this package's `components/mate/Firstmate.jsx` mock predates the eyes and emotes). Base states: idle = near-still drift (ice cyan) with occasional fidgets; listening = the tesseract shapeshifts flat into two counter-rotating hexagons (Interstellar-robot style) breathing with the voice, spun faster by keystrokes — typing holds listening exactly like voice; working = fast double rotation, shimmer, pulsing nodes. The ember (`--wire-hot`) rides a separate busy parameter, not the state — hot means the agent's own turn is running, even mid-listening, and it cools in place when the turn ends. One-shot emotes overlay the base states and return home on their own: greet (bow + wink on app open), celebrate (spin burst + sparks, on a landed task), ponder, confused (stutter + jitter, on a failed turn), and a fidget pool (roll, yawn, orbit, pretend black hole) drawn at random, also on a tap. Transitions are continuous morphs with named clips. Big and central in null state; stays in place behind the cards (dimmed, faintly blurred) while they show, so finishing the stack reveals him again. Voice activation is keybind-only — a plain click on the input focuses it for typing.
- **Cards, not chat** — agent responses arrive as a prioritized stack of cards, one shown at a time. A card can be a decision, a task result, a live prototype, etc. No message bubbles ever.
- **Tasks** — every ask the captain makes lands in a task record (`FM3K-12` keys, one project per managed repo plus Scratch). The captain reads the record in two places and writes it in none: the **now panel** (right side rail; `components/now/NowPanel`) is what IS - a counts line with a `filter` affordance, rows for "waiting on you" and "underway", and "to land" / "charted" / "landed · 7d" collapsed to a count; minimal by default, everything richer behind a click. Clicking a row opens the task's **record card** (`ResponseCard` kind `record`, body `components/cards/TaskRecord`): goal, the captain's words verbatim, graph, latest report, timeline tail, delivery - read-only, no buttons, its only control is close. Every write, from a steer to a stop to a merge, happens by talking to Firstmate; an open record card is what points the turn at that task.
- **Crewmates** — background workers Firstmate delegates to. Rendered as 3D wireframe **tetrahedra** — the simplest solid, deliberately simpler than the 4D Firstmate (dimensional hierarchy = org hierarchy). Only a small overview strip (n working / n idle); never a focal point. Above the strip, an **ActivityFeed** thread logs major crewmate events (spawn / report / decommission) — chromeless 1px rail, hh:mm mono timestamps, rows fading with age, newest at the bottom, a thin left-edge thumb on the rail and a top dissolve when history outgrows the column. Both live in the left side rail as host-framed panels (the feed fills the rail height the strip leaves; a feed row wraps to at most two lines at the rail's width); with nothing to show they are absent, and so is the rail.
- **Side rails** - two dock columns, left and right, framing the stage (character, cards, input) on the home view. Empty by default and invisible when empty: zero width, no border, no header, no affordance, so a window with nothing docked is pixel-identical to one without rails. A rail is a vertical stack of host-framed panels at one fixed width (`--rail-width`, never resizable); the host owns each panel's title, attribution, and collapse, and a panel styles only its body region. The stage insets and is never covered. Rails carry contributed UX (the plugin system's `side-panel` slot); the app's own feed and crew strip are the first two panels, on the left, and the now panel is the one panel on the right. A panel declares its size: `content` hugs what it shows, `fill` takes the rail height its siblings leave. The app never attributes its own panels; a third party's panel carries its name in the header.
- **Subscriptions** - users add AI subscriptions (Claude, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Grok, Kimi…). The app discovers each subscription's models; you place them in four slots - premium, high, medium, low - and a starter placement is filled in when a subscription connects; it routes tasks by slot and remaining quota. Users can override model choice.
- **Machines** — SSH hosts the user pools; the app tracks specs and utilization and places tasks.

## Sources
- Quota-tracking domain model: https://github.com/kunchenguid/quota-axi (src/types.ts, src/pace.ts) — provider ids, quota windows, pace/runway/burn-multiple semantics, intelligence buckets.
- No Figma, codebase, or brand assets were provided. **There is no logo**: render "Firstmate 3000" in plain type (Space Grotesk 500) wherever a mark would go. All visuals here are original.

## CONTENT FUNDAMENTALS
- **Tone:** calm, competent, low-ceremony. The app talks like a trusted first officer: brief status, clear options, no exclamation points, no cheerleading.
- **Casing:** sentence case everywhere, including buttons ("Add subscription", "Submit"). Micro-labels are uppercase with wide tracking (`CREW`, `QUOTA`, `ON PACE`).
- **Person:** the app addresses the user as "you"; Firstmate refers to itself sparingly and never says "I'm excited". Task copy is factual: "Refactor finished. 14 files changed."
- **Numbers & data** are always mono (JetBrains Mono): quotas, percentages, host specs, keybinds.
- **Emoji:** never.
- **Examples:** placeholder — "press/hold right ⌥ to talk"; decision card title — "Two ways to fix the flaky test"; crew strip — "3 working · 5 idle"; quota — "62% left · on pace · resets Fri".
- **Card bodies:** semantic HTML in a sandboxed iframe, never one unstructured paragraph. Prefer short headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, and purposeful visual layouts. The host retains kind, title, close, pager, and footer actions. Use design tokens only: body `--text-base` / `--fg-2`; headings `--text-md` or `--text-base` / `--fg-1` / weight 500; code `--font-mono` / `--text-sm` / `--fg-1`; links `--accent`. Scripts and external resources are forbidden; `data-fm-action` may mirror a declared host action.

## VISUAL FOUNDATIONS
- **Palette:** deep-space blue-black base (`--bg-0 #05070d`), ice-cyan accent (`--accent #7fdcff`) = the Firstmate's light. Exactly two chromatic families: ice cyan for everything calm (accent, ok, medium bucket) and ember/lava (`--hot #ffa257`, `--danger #ff6b52`) for the occasional hot thing — energy, sun, fire: warnings, high-intelligence bucket, the working Firstmate. Everything else is neutral gray. Light theme via `[data-theme="light"]`. One accent on screen at a time; large areas are always near-black (or near-white in light).
- **Type:** Space Grotesk (UI/display, weights 300–600); JetBrains Mono (data). Display is light (300–400) and large with tight tracking; labels are 11px uppercase tracked +0.09em.

- The left rail carries the activity feed and the crew strip as two Tier-2 side panels (phase 2, below); the right rail carries the now panel (task-system P4, below), the one panel the captain chose for it.

## D5: the two side rails

Home view: `[rail-left] [stage] [rail-right]` as one flex row (`App.tsx`); the stage holds the fixed geometry the app always had. Six rules, each with its test:

| Rule | Where it holds | Test |
|---|---|---|
| Empty means invisible and zero-width; the window is pixel-identical to today's | `Rail` renders an empty element when no panel has content; `[data-rail]:empty` (design/styles.css) sets width and padding to 0 | `Rail.test.tsx`; `tests/e2e/side-rails.spec.ts` compares a screenshot with the rails present and empty against one with the rail nodes removed, byte for byte |
| The stage insets; it is never covered | the stage is `flex: 1` beside fixed-width rails, and is a container (`cqw`) for anything that must not assume it is the window | `side-rails.spec.ts` lets the first feed line dock the real panels and measures stage x/width and the character and input centres |
| One rail width token, not resizable | `--rail-width` (skill and app `tokens/spacing.css`); `resize: none`; no resize affordance exists | `side-rails.spec.ts` |
| A rail is a vertical stack of panels; the host owns title, attribution, and collapse; the plugin styles only the body | `SidePanelChrome` renders title/attribution from manifest data and the collapse control; the body sits in `[data-side-panel-body]`; collapse state is host-owned (`railStore.ts`); the host's own panels carry no attribution (the app never names itself) | `Rail.test.tsx`; `side-rails.spec.ts` collapses a real panel and finds no attribution on the built-in ones |
| Home view only in v1 | `App.tsx` renders rails only when `view === "home"` | `side-rails.spec.ts` |
| The host caps mounts (3 per rail) and refuses overflow loudly | `RAIL_MOUNT_CAP`; the side-panel registry's admission hook throws a `ContributionError` naming the rail, its panels, and the refused contribution | `host.test.ts` |

**Visibility is data, not a verb.** A side panel binds a `PanelSource<T>` (`subscribe` + `get`, framework-free); `null` means nothing to show, and the host renders no chrome for it. There is no `show_panel` / `hide_panel` anywhere, and none is planned. Placement: a contribution declares a preferred side, an order, and a `size` (`content` hugs what it shows; `fill` takes the rail height its siblings leave); `placeSidePanels` honours the side in v1 and sorts by order, then id.

## D6: the capability posture

The finding stands as the proposal put it: letting a Jira plugin fetch Jira needs a mediated verb, not a relaxed sandbox. **Phase 0 lands the declaration side only.**

# Project agent memory

This file is the project's committed home for project-intrinsic agent knowledge: build, test, release, architecture, and sharp-edge notes that should travel with the code.

## What this project is

Firstmate 3000 is a local-only Electron desktop app: a calm AI first-officer that routes work to the user's own LLM subscriptions (Codex, Copilot, Grok, Claude Max, Cursor, Kimi, OpenRouter, ...). No SaaS, no hosted backend, no account system from us. Product vision, interaction model, and constraints: `.claude/skills/firstmate-3000-design/readme.md`.

## Standing product principle (captain, 2026-08-17)

FM3000 is the most advanced agent harness, but it aggressively hides that complexity from the end user. The user interacts with just the main Firstmate agent and a few settings - nothing else. The fewer concepts we expose, the better. Accounts, harnesses, crewmate transports, quota routing, and rebinding are machinery; the surfaces a person touches stay calm. Concretely: the sign-in flow and the Subscriptions tab never expose the "harness" technicality - they speak only of providers, accounts (labeled by the user), and quota. An e2e assertion enforces the wording.

## Design system (mandatory)

All UI work MUST follow the project skill `firstmate-3000-design` (`.claude/skills/firstmate-3000-design/`). It owns every visual and interaction rule: tokens, type, color, motion, components, character rendering, tone of copy. Never re-invent brand rules in code; if a rule is missing, extend the skill first, then implement. The package is offline-complete (fonts and mock runtime vendored; see its readme "Offline completeness").

- Tokens: `.claude/skills/firstmate-3000-design/tokens/*.css` - consume these, never hardcode values they define.
- Click-through mock of the whole app: serve the skill dir over HTTP (any static server), open `ui_kits/firstmate/index.html`. Voice states trigger on a real right-⌥ keydown.

## Architecture and implementation

The architecture is **decided** (captain sign-off 2026-08-13, decision record in `docs/architecture.md` §14 - do not relitigate). Implementers start from `docs/implementation-plan.md`, which orders the build into phases with acceptance checks and names the house reference repos to mirror (Pi SDK, hi-bit, baby-menu, pi-launcher). If reality contradicts a recorded decision, escalate with `needs-decision` instead of improvising. Current build status vs the plan: `docs/mvp-status.md`.

## Working on the code

- Green gate on every commit: `pnpm typecheck && pnpm check && pnpm lint:adherence && pnpm test`, then `pnpm build && pnpm exec playwright test` for the e2e suite. The adherence lint runs the design skill's `_adherence.oxlintrc.json` through ESLint FlatCompat (current oxlint cannot execute its selector rules); its raw-px/hex rules are warn-level by the skill's own design.
- Standing CI rule (PR 8): CI green only if every check on the exact head commit SHA reports status=completed and conclusion=success (use `gh pr checks`). One green `checks` job never suffices while `package-smoke` or others pend/fail. Never treat old SHAs as authoritative for the current head.
- E2E runs are hermetic and windowless: `tests/e2e/launch.ts` gives each app a throwaway userData and HOME (`FM3000_USER_DATA_DIR` keeps the window hidden - captain directive), fake media devices (no macOS mic prompt), a mock OpenAI-compatible provider wired through app-scoped `models.json` (`tests/e2e/mockProvider.ts`), and faked voice-model readiness (opt out with `voiceModelReady: false`). Quota fixtures ride `FM3000_QUOTA_FIXTURE_DIR`. Claude credentials seed into that HOME's `.claude` (`prepareHome`), never a per-account vault store.
- `flag_missed_escalation` (PoC-2 capture C3, `src/core/pi/supervisionTools.ts`) is the only path from "you should have told me about that" to a durable label: under-escalation is otherwise unobservable, because a routine verdict is one feed line and no captain contact. It stamps migration 16's nullable `missed_escalation`/`missed_note`/`missed_at` on the task's newest routine `supervision_outcomes` row (or a named `#id` from `supervision_log`), write-once, `routine`-only, and captain-turn gated by the same wake stamp `remember` uses - the label's value is that the captain confirmed it, so the agent cannot manufacture one on a scheduled or supervision wake. Refusals are tool text, never throws. No card, no setting, no user surface.
- The retrospective miss deriver (PoC-2 capture C2, `scripts/derive-miss-candidates.ts`, `docs/miss-deriver.md`) is an OFFLINE tables-only scan: for every `supervision_outcomes` `routine` verdict it looks forward in a window (default 24h) for a later captain verdict, a host-written `turn_failed` / task-failure wake, a captain-resolved card, or a captain steer/interrupt on that task, and emits weak candidate-miss JSONL. Never writes C3's `missed_escalation`/`missed_note`/`missed_at`. Inputs are parameters (`--db`/`--user-data`/`--window-hours`) so a MacBook-exported `firstmate.db` runs identically. Fixture-tested; no live data required.
- The dispatch extractor (PoC-2 capture C5, `scripts/extract-dispatch-corpus.ts`, `docs/dispatch-extractor.md`) is an OFFLINE dev tool over data the app already writes: Pi session JSONL joined to `tasks`/`repos`/`cards`, emitting the six-way classify-first turns as a weakly-labelled JSONL corpus. No schema change, no product surface, nothing leaves the box. Its inputs are all parameters (`--user-data`/`--sessions`/`--db`) so another machine's exported userData runs identically. C2, C4, and C5 are the `scripts/*.ts` files: Node 24 type-strips them with no build step, which is why their relative imports carry an explicit `.ts` and `tsconfig.node.json` sets `allowImportingTsExtensions`.

The key failure: character center is 150px off from window center. That's exactly half a rail width (300/2 = 150). So `position: fixed` is NOT working as viewport-relative!
The root cause is clear: `container-type: inline-size` on the stage is turning it into a containing block for the fixed-position character and input, so they’re still being positioned relative to the stage instead of the viewport. That’s why the 150 px offset appears exactly when the left rail is open.

To fix it we have to break that containment chain for the character/input without losing the container-type benefits for the cards that need cqw.

Best minimal-change approach (Option 5 above):

1. Keep `container-type: inline-size` only on an inner wrapper around the cards that need it.
2. Move the character and input outside the stage entirely—make them siblings of the flex row, full-window absolute positioned, and only visible/pointer-events-active when the stage is active.
3. Use the CSS variables we already discussed to compute the offset.

Two classes of failures:
The flex container is swallowing clicks because it’s positioned absolutely over the stage and doesn’t have `pointer-events: none`. That’s why taps on the character never reach HomeMate.

Quick fix: add `pointerEvents: "none"` to the flex row, and make sure the rails themselves have `pointerEvents: " auto"` (either inline or via `[data-rail]` CSS).

For the now-panel test, the conflict is that the test expects the input to stay inside the stage on narrow windows, but the user wants it window-centered. The cleanest resolution is to make HomePrompt’s width shrink with the rails so that a 328 px input at 960 px still centers inside the stage (316–644). Use the `:has` trick on body to set `--rail-left` and `--rail-right` dynamically, then update `STAGE_WIDTH` to:

```css
min(560px, calc(100vw - var(--rail-left 0px) - var(--rail-right 0px) - 2 * var(--space-4)))
```

That should make both tests happy.
